text:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV-cache metadata growth > 1.8GB/min across paged pools in eu-west-1. Auto-mitigation triggered: rate-limit new continuous-batch admissions. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/kv-metadata-buildup :rotating_light:
Maya Patel: seeing huge tail latencies for inference-hosts, up to 2.2s p99 for short prompts. customer-facing errors for AcmePay. tagging SRE and runtime.
Sam Chen: pulling heap + metadata counters now. index_metadata_bytes is spiking, block-manager allocated blocks increasing but not freed. likely metadata leak or batch path holding references.
Jordan Lee: this coincided with the scheduler change we rolled yesterday (continuous-batching v2). I want an immediate feature-flag rollback if we can.
Nora Alvarez: AcmePay is on a dedicated pool in eu-west-1. SLA alerts firing. Customer success is on call, prepping message.
Priya Singh: I can limit the batching window + cap continuous-batch size quickly. If we reduce continuous batch admit window from 200ms -> 50ms it should cut parallel inflight batches and free metadata pressure.
Andre Gomez: we should also eject stale metadata aggressively until we get a safer config. I have an eviction script ready to run against the affected node set.
oncall-bot: On-call handoff: @Maya Patel is active primary, @Sam Chen secondary. Please update the incident log.
Maya Patel: Ok quick plan: 1) rollback feature flag for continuous-batching-v2 2) immediate config override (batch_window_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=1024, metadata_limit_bytes=500000000) 3) run targeted metadata eviction 4) follow-up hotfix to block-manager serialization leak.
Sam Chen: metrics snapshot (snippet):
```
kv_pool/metadata_bytes_total {node="kv-pg-14"} 3245123456
kv_pool/allocated_blocks_total {node="kv-pg-14"} 4821
kv_pool/evicted_blocks_total {node="kv-pg-14"} 12
batcher/inflight_batches {node="kv-pg-14"} 78
```
Sam Chen: you can see evicted_blocks is tiny vs allocated -> not freeing.
Jordan Lee: rolling the FF rollback now. curl to admin API: `curl -X POST https://admin.prod.redwood/api/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"name":"continuous_batching_v2","value":false}'`
Jordan Lee: also doing a `kubectl rollout undo deployment/batcher -n inference` for the canary we promoted.
Priya Singh: config override (applied via config service):
```
{
  "batch_window_ms": "50",
  "max_batch_tokens": "1024",
  "enable_prefix_cache": "true",
  "prefix_cache_ttl_ms": "300000",
  "metadata_limit_bytes": "500000000"
}
```
Priya Singh: sent override, should propagate to nodes in ~30s.
Andre Gomez: running targeted eviction now on nodes [kv-pg-12, kv-pg-13, kv-pg-14]: `/opt/tools/evict_metadata.sh --nodes kv-pg-12,kv-pg-13,kv-pg-14 --threshold 200000000`
Andre Gomez: eviction logs:
```
[evict] node=kv-pg-14 evicted=120 metadata_freed=312000000
[evict] node=kv-pg-13 evicted=90 metadata_freed=240000000
[evict] node=kv-pg-12 evicted=75 metadata_freed=180000000
```
Maya Patel: after rollback + eviction: p99 latency dropped to 320ms on affected hosts, metadata growth rate down to ~60MB/min. Not fully stable yet but much better.
Nora Alvarez: reporting to AcmePay: "We observed an internal KV metadata surge impacting latency; we've applied mitigations (rollback + config cap) and are monitoring. We expect normal service within 30-60 minutes."
Sam Chen: noticed one node still has a persistent metadata allocation trace in logs: `blockmgr: failed to release metadata ref count: id=0x7f23f2`. This looks like a serialization/deser path not decrementing ref on certain error flows.
Jordan Lee: assigning a hotfix: I'm going to patch block-manager to add hedged `decrement_ref` in finally blocks and add a regression test for continuous-batch abort paths.
Jordan Lee: patch draft: `git push origin hotfix/blockmgr-refcount-ensure && gh pr create --fill`
Priya Singh: follow-ups: 1) add size-aware eviction (cap on metadata bytes per pool) 2) telemetry alert for metadata growth rate > 100MB/min 3) run a canary of continuous-batching-v2 behind a stricter admission controller.
Maya Patel: ops checklist for next 24h: - keep continuous-batching-v2 off - monitor eu-west-1 pool metrics - incremental rollout once hotfix validated - notify customers in status page if regression reappears.
Andre Gomez: I've scheduled an ad-hoc canary run with synthetic traffic to validate patch; will post results in 30m.
Sam Chen: monitors back to green for p99, continuing 5m cadence checks.
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: please update #incidents with timeline and root-cause when available.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone. tagging for postmortem: @Jordan Lee (root cause & fix), @Priya Singh (config mitigations), @Sam Chen (monitoring & telemetry), @Andre Gomez (eviction script). I'll create the incident doc after stabilization. :heavy_check_mark:
